## 1. Incident summary

During operations at an underground coal mine, an **uncontrolled fall of ground (roof/strata failure)** occurred in a **development heading**. **One** person — **the Deceased (role: development-heading miner)** — sustained fatal injuries. This is a **fatal accident** and, on the confirmed facts, a **DGMS-reportable event** (see §8).

The material unwanted event (MUE) is: **uncontrolled fall of roof/side strata onto a person in an underground coal roadway.** By the outcome alone, the mine's **ground-control (strata-support) critical control did not perform its safety function** at the point and time of the event — a person was exposed to strata of sufficient energy to be fatal in a location where the control system existed to prevent exactly that exposure. **Why** the control failed is the subject of §5–§6 and is not yet established.

**Facts confirmed at role level (do not require further evidence to state):**
- The event was a fall of ground / strata failure (roof fall).
- It occurred in a development heading (an advancing single-entry/roadway environment).
- One person was fatally injured.
- The mine is an underground coal mine.

**Everything else is a `[GAP]`** and is routed to the investigation team below. No mechanism, measurement, time, or human action beyond the above has been supplied and none is invented here.

## 5. Critical control analysis — strata support (absent-or-failed critical controls)

For a fall-of-ground fatality, the relevant **critical controls** are the barriers that keep a person from being exposed to unsupported or failing ground. Because a person was fatally struck by falling strata, **at least one critical control failed to perform**. Each control is assessed as *present & effective* / *present but failed* / *absent* / **`[GAP]`** pending evidence. This is the honest current state: the **failure of the overall ground-control barrier system is established by the outcome**; **which** specific control failed is a line of inquiry.

| CC | Critical control (strata management) | Intended function | Performance at T-0 | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CC-1 | **Geotechnical characterisation & adverse-ground hazard mapping** | Identify weak/variable ground before it is exposed and set support to suit | `[GAP]` — did the plan foresee the ground encountered? | E-5, E-12 |
| CC-2 | **Support design adequate for the ground** (Systematic Support Rules) | Support pattern/length/density matched to rock-mass conditions | `[GAP]` — design adequacy unverified | E-2, E-5 |
| CC-3 | **Support installed to design, to cycle, before advance/entry** | No person under unsupported/inadequately-supported roof | `[GAP]` — as-installed vs design unverified | E-3, E-1 |
| CC-4 | **Strata monitoring + Trigger Action Response Plan (TARP)** | Detect movement/deterioration and trigger withdrawal/extra support | `[GAP]` — readings, triggers and response unverified | E-4 |
| CC-5 | **Exclusion — no entry under newly exposed / unsupported roof** | Keep persons out of the fall zone until supported | **Failed or breached in effect** — a person was in the fall zone at T-0; *why* is `[GAP]` (control absent, not followed, or defeated by an unforeseen failure) | E-1, E-3, E-7 |
| CC-6 | **Competent statutory inspection** (deputy/sirdar/overman pre- & during-shift) | Detect drummy/loose/moving ground and act before failure | `[GAP]` — inspection scope/findings/actions unverified | E-6 |
| CC-7 | **Support materials & roof-bolting plant available and serviceable** | Enable support to be installed to cycle without delay | `[GAP]` — availability at the time unverified | E-8 |

**Established critical-control finding.** The **fall-of-ground barrier system did not prevent a person's fatal exposure to failing strata** (CC-5 did not deliver its outcome). The controlling defect(s) among CC-1…CC-7 are **not yet identified** and must be determined from E-1…E-8 before the CAPA in §7 is finalised. This finding is defensible from the confirmed facts without assuming any specific mechanism.

## 6. ICAM causal analysis

ICAM organises contributing factors across four levels, from the point of failure outward to the systemic/latent conditions. Per method and quality gate, the analysis **must reach organisational factors** and **must not stop at "miner error."** Each factor below is tagged **[FINDING]** (logically established) or **[LINE OF INQUIRY / `[GAP]`]** (candidate factor to be tested against the cited evidence). Candidate factors are the recognised failure pathways for roof falls in development headings — listed so evidence collection is targeted, **not** asserted as what happened.

### 6.1 Absent / failed defences (the last lines of defence)
- **[FINDING]** The ground-control barrier system did not keep the Deceased out of the fall zone / did not hold the strata (§5). *(Cites E-1; outcome-established.)*
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Support design not matched to the ground actually encountered (design gap). *(E-2, E-5)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Support installed short of design — pattern/length/density/timing (installation gap). *(E-3)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Strata monitoring absent, not read, or its TARP triggers not acted on (detection gap). *(E-4)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Statutory pre-/during-shift inspection did not detect or act on adverse-ground indicators (inspection gap). *(E-6)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Exclusion/standing-back from unsupported roof not enforced by physical/procedural means. *(E-3, E-7)* `[GAP]`

### 6.2 Individual / team actions (the "sharp end" — context, not blame)
> The Deceased is a **victim of a system failure**; "miner error" is **rejected** as a stopping point. Any action at this level is only a valid contributing factor when the system that shaped it is traced (6.3–6.4).
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** A person was in the fall zone at T-0 — establish *why* (task requirement, no alternative safe position, ground appeared sound, exclusion not physically possible with the method in use). *(E-1, E-7)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Support cycle / advance sequence at the moment of the event (was advance ahead of support, or within an assumed-supported zone that failed?). *(E-3, E-11)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Any adverse-ground indicator seen and how it was interpreted/escalated by the crew and supervisor. *(E-4, E-6, E-7)* `[GAP]`

### 6.3 Task / environmental (workplace) conditions
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Geological anomaly at the location — fault, slip, roll, sandstone channel, kettlebottom, slickensided parting, or water-weakened roof. *(E-5)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Variable/weak roof not reflected in the support standard for that stretch. *(E-2, E-5)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Support materials or roof-bolting plant unavailable/unserviceable, delaying support to cycle. *(E-8)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Roadway width/height, lighting, dust or visibility limiting detection of loose/moving roof. *(E-1, E-7)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** Development single-entry geometry limiting safe standing positions and escape. *(E-1)* `[GAP]`

### 6.4 Organisational factors (systemic / latent conditions — the investigation must land here)
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** **Strata/ground-control management plan and Systematic Support Rules** — adequacy, currency, and whether they cover variable ground and a change-of-conditions trigger. *(E-12, E-2)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** **Strata-monitoring & TARP system design** — is monitoring specified, resourced, read, trended, and does the TARP mandate withdrawal on trigger? *(E-4)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** **Supervision & statutory-inspection regime** — competency, workload, and effectiveness of deputy/sirdar/overman examinations for detecting strata deterioration. *(E-6, E-10)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** **Competence & training** for ground-recognition and support installation across the relevant roles. *(E-10)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** **Production vs. safety pressure** — advance-rate expectations, cycle discipline, and whether "support before advance" could be traded away under pressure. *(E-11)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** **Management of change for adverse ground** — is there a defined trigger and process to revise support when ground worsens? *(E-12)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** **Resourcing & maintenance** of support materials and roof-bolting plant. *(E-8)* `[GAP]`
- **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** **Learning from prior events** — were previous falls/convergence/dangerous-occurrences (Form J) acted on with effective, verified controls? *(E-9)* `[GAP]`

### 6.5 Causal summary & cause → evidence traceability

| Cause ID | Level (ICAM) | Statement | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **RC-0** | Defence (outcome) | The ground-control barrier system failed to prevent fatal exposure to failing strata | **[FINDING]** | E-1 |
| RC-1 | Task/Environment | Adverse/variable ground condition at the location | Line of inquiry | E-5 |
| RC-2 | Failed defence | Support design and/or installation not adequate for the ground | Line of inquiry | E-2, E-3, E-5 |
| RC-3 | Failed defence | Strata deterioration not detected / not acted on (monitoring + inspection) | Line of inquiry | E-4, E-6 |
| RC-4 | Failed defence | Exclusion from the fall zone not effective | Line of inquiry | E-1, E-3, E-7 |
| RC-5 | **Organisational** | Ground-control management plan / Support Rules / TARP inadequate or not enforced | Line of inquiry (systemic) | E-12, E-2, E-4 |
| RC-6 | **Organisational** | Supervision, competence, resourcing, MOC, or production-pressure latent conditions | Line of inquiry (systemic) | E-6, E-8, E-10, E-11 |
| RC-7 | **Organisational** | Prior-event learning not converted into effective controls | Line of inquiry (systemic) | E-9 |

> **ICAM completeness note:** the analysis **reaches organisational factors** (RC-5…RC-7). Confirmation of which candidate causes are actual requires E-1…E-12; the systemic level must **not** be closed out until the plan, monitoring, supervision, resourcing and learning factors have each been evidenced or excluded.

## 7. Corrective & preventive actions (hierarchy-of-controls ranked)

Actions are grounded in **ISO 45001 cl. 10.2** (incident, nonconformity & corrective action) and the **hierarchy of controls** (ISO 45001 cl. 8.1.2). They fall in two tiers: **immediate/interim controls** — defensible now, independent of the confirmed mechanism, to prevent recurrence while the investigation runs — and **systemic controls**, which are provisional and must be **confirmed or revised** once RC-1…RC-7 are evidenced. Owners are **role labels**; dates are working targets for the competent person to ratify.

### Tier 1 — Immediate / interim (do not wait for root cause)

| # | Action | HoC level | Owner (role) | Due |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CA-1 | **Suspend development in the affected heading** and any comparable-ground headings; do not resume until a competent person re-authorises | Elimination (of exposure) | Mine Manager | 7 July 2026 |
| CA-2 | **Preserve the scene and evidence** (cavity, fallen strata, installed support, monitoring instruments) for the investigation/DGMS inquiry | Administrative | Investigation Team Lead | 7 July 2026 |
| CA-3 | **Physically prohibit entry under unsupported/newly-exposed roof** across the mine (barriers/temporary standing support / no-go marking), pending review | Engineering | Undermanager | 8 July 2026 |
| CA-4 | **Re-inspect all active development/faces** for strata condition (drummy/loose/moving roof, telltale movement); withdraw and support any at-risk area | Administrative | Mining Sirdar / Shift Overman | 8 July 2026 |
| CA-5 | **Reissue and brief the "support before advance / stand-back from unsupported roof" rule** to all underground crews (toolbox brief, de-identified) | Administrative | Safety Officer | 9 July 2026 |

### Tier 2 — Systemic (provisional — confirm/adjust after RC-1…RC-7 are evidenced)

| # | Action | Addresses | HoC level | Owner (role) | Due |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CA-6 | **Re-survey geotechnical/ground conditions** for the panel and re-derive the Systematic Support Rules to suit the ground actually present (incl. adverse-ground provisions) | RC-1, RC-2, RC-5 | Engineering | Strata-Control/Geotechnical Engineer | 21 July 2026 |
| CA-7 | Where reasonably practicable, **reduce the need for persons at the exposed face** (e.g. remote/mechanised installation, temporary roof-support systems that support from a protected position) | RC-4 | Elimination/Substitution | Mine Manager | 30 September 2026 |
| CA-8 | **Upgrade the strata-monitoring regime and TARP** — specify instruments, reading frequency, trend review, and mandatory withdrawal triggers with named responders | RC-3, RC-5 | Engineering + Administrative | Strata-Control/Geotechnical Engineer | 21 August 2026 |
| CA-9 | **Strengthen statutory pre-/during-shift examination** for strata deterioration — checklist, competency check, and closed-loop action recording | RC-3, RC-6 | Administrative | Undermanager | 21 August 2026 |
| CA-10 | **Assure support-materials and roof-bolting-plant availability** (minimum stock, maintenance/standby regime) so support is never deferred for want of resources | RC-6 | Engineering | Undermanager | 21 August 2026 |
| CA-11 | **Ground-recognition & support-installation competency refresh** for sirdars, overmen and support crews | RC-6 | Administrative | Training Officer | 30 September 2026 |
| CA-12 | **Management-of-change trigger for adverse ground** — a defined process to revise support/monitoring when conditions worsen, with a stop-and-fix authority at the frontline | RC-5 | Administrative | Mine Manager | 30 September 2026 |
| CA-13 | **Production/safety-pressure review** — verify advance-rate targets cannot override "support before advance"; make cycle discipline auditable | RC-6 | Administrative | Colliery Agent | 31 October 2026 |
| CA-14 | **Review closure of prior fall/convergence/dangerous-occurrence actions** (Form J & internal) and re-open any not effectively controlled | RC-7 | Administrative | Safety Officer | 31 October 2026 |
| CA-15 | **Effectiveness verification** — audit that CA-6…CA-14 are implemented and are working (not just closed); report to management review | all | Administrative | Investigation Team Lead | 31 December 2026 |

> **Lower-order-control flag.** Several Tier-2 items are administrative (CA-9, CA-11, CA-12, CA-13, CA-14). These are retained only **alongside** the higher-order engineering/elimination controls (CA-6, CA-7, CA-8, CA-10). Any administrative action that ends up standing **alone** for a given hazard must carry a documented justification of why elimination/substitution/engineering is not reasonably practicable, **or be escalated** — the competent person must not accept an admin-only treatment of the roof-fall hazard.

**CAPA → cause traceability** is shown in the "Addresses" column; every Tier-2 action maps to a numbered cause (RC-1…RC-7), and every confirmed cause must carry at least one closing action before the investigation is signed off.

## 8. Statutory notification & reportability (DGMS pointer)

**Grounding:** Mines Act 1952 / applicable Coal Mines Regulations (India), administered by DGMS through **regional/zonal offices**; `KB-REG-IN-DGMS`. **Region/zone resolution is mandatory before any form is routed** and is currently **`[GAP]`** (F2). Jurisdiction is treated as **India/DGMS** for this pointer; if the mine is **not** in India, the reportability path differs and must be re-resolved `[GAP]`.

**Reportability verdict:** a **fatal accident** is a **DGMS-reportable event**. The following instruments apply:

| Obligation | Instrument (verified anchor) | Timing | Status / action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Accident notification | **24-hour accident notice** (serious/fatal/dangerous occurrence) | **within 24 hours** of the event | Clock runs from the incident datetime (**F1 `[GAP]`**). **Confirm the notice has been served to the correct DGMS regional/zonal office** and record when. Owner: **Mine Manager** |
| Accident register | **Form J** — accident & dangerous-occurrence register | maintained current | **Enter this fatal accident in Form J** and cross-check prior related entries (E-9). Owner: **Safety Officer** |

**`[GAP]` / do-not-invent items (route to a DGMS-qualified competent person):**
- The **specific numbered accident-notice form id** — `(DGMS-prescribed — verify per mine)` **`[GAP]`**. The 24-hour duty and timing are verified; the exact numbered form is not asserted here.
- The **DGMS regional/zonal office** to receive the notice — **`[GAP]`** (depends on F2; a wrong-zone filing is a misfiled statutory notice).
- The **exact section/regulation numbers** of the Mines Act 1952 / Coal Mines Regulations governing notice, inquiry and any court-of-inquiry trigger — **`[GAP]`**; confirm with the DGMS-qualified competent person. Not invented here.
- **OSH-Code transition note (legacy-first):** the Mines Act 1952 is among the laws being subsumed by the **OSH Code 2020**; commencement is state-by-state and pending. Continue with the **legacy DGMS forms** the mine files today and confirm current status at filing. **`[GAP]` — confirm commencement status for the mine's state.**

## 9. Lessons learned / broader learnings

1. **A fatal roof fall is, by definition, a critical-control failure of the ground-control system** — the investigation's value is in finding *which* control failed and *why the system allowed it*, not in attributing the person's presence in the fall zone to "error."
2. **Development headings concentrate roof-fall risk** — a person near a freshly exposed, single-entry face has few safe standing positions; controls that keep people out of the fall zone (CC-5, CA-7) are the highest-value defences and should be pursued as engineering/elimination, not procedure alone.
3. **"Support before advance" only protects if it cannot be traded away** — support design adequacy, materials availability, and freedom from production pressure (RC-2, RC-6) determine whether the rule holds at 3 a.m. under a tight cycle.
4. **Detection is a control, not paperwork** — strata monitoring and statutory examinations only prevent falls if readings are trended and a TARP forces withdrawal on a trigger (CA-8). A monitoring system with no mandated response is not a control.
5. **Adverse ground needs a change trigger** — variable geology (faults, rolls, kettlebottoms) is foreseeable in coal; the absence of a management-of-change trigger for worsening ground (CA-12) is a recurring latent condition in fall-of-ground fatalities.
6. **Close the learning loop** — prior falls/convergence/dangerous occurrences (Form J, E-9) are the cheapest warnings available; unclosed or ineffective prior actions (RC-7) are a systemic red flag to test in every such investigation.

- This report is built **only** on the confirmed facts in §1 (fatal roof fall; development heading; one fatality; underground coal mine). **No mechanism, measurement, time, or human action has been invented.** All specific determinations are **`[GAP]`** and routed to the investigation team (§2, §4).
- Causal statements are either **[FINDING]** (established by the outcome) or **[LINE OF INQUIRY]** (candidate factors to test against evidence). The candidate factors are the recognised roof-fall pathways, listed to target evidence collection — they are **not** conclusions.
- **De-identification** was applied first; the Deceased and all personnel appear only as role labels; no small-count (<5) cell or re-identification key appears here.
- `incident_rates` were **not** computed (no exposure hours/counts supplied); any rate would be fabricated and is withheld.
- **This is decision-support and a working draft. It must be reviewed and signed off by a DGMS-qualified competent person and is subject to the statutory DGMS inquiry.** It is not itself a competent-person sign-off, a statutory finding, or legal advice. The corrective actions in §7 are provisional recommendations for that competent person to ratify, re-sequence, or replace once the causes are evidenced.
